PEOPLE v. BALDWIN
The Rust Shooting Case (2021)

2
What happened
  • October 21, 2021, Rust set, New Mexico
  • A prop revolver held by Alec Baldwin fired a live round
  • Halyna Hutchins (cinematographer) was killed and Joel Souza (director) was wounded
3
The Rust set
  • A low-budget Western filmed at Bonanza Creek Ranch, near Santa Fe
  • An inexperienced production team and armorer
  • Earlier accidental gun discharges on set
  • Crew walked off over safety conditions
4
Who was involved
Alec Baldwinactor and producer, holding the gun
Hannah Gutierrez-Reedarmorer, who loaded the gun
Dave Hallsassistant director, who handed over the gun and said “cold gun”
Seth Kenneyammunition supplier (PDQ Arm & Prop)
Sarah Zachryprop master
5
How the live round
got into the gun
  • The gun was loaded with six rounds believed to be dummies
  • The checks were incomplete, by both the armorer and the assistant director
  • The fatal round came from a “dummy” box that held live rounds
  • Six live rounds were found on set in total
  • The source was never proven
6

7
Criminal Charges Against Baldwin
January 2023
Baldwin charged with involuntary manslaughter.
April 2023
Charges dropped pending further investigation.
January 2024
Baldwin charged again with involuntary manslaughter.
July 2024
Trial began in New Mexico.
8
Why Was Baldwin's
Trial Dismissed?
  • July 12, 2024: Prosecutors failed to share important ammunition evidence with Baldwin's lawyers.
  • Brady v. Maryland (1963): Prosecutors must disclose material evidence favorable to the defence.
  • Dismissed with prejudice: The judge considered the violation serious enough to prevent the same charge from being brought again.
  • No verdict: Baldwin was neither found guilty nor not guilty.

10
Actus Reus
  • Voluntary act: drawing, pointing and cocking the revolver were willed movements (MPC § 2.01)
  • State v. Decina: liability can rest on an earlier voluntary act, even if the trigger pull is disputed
  • Omission: not checking the gun counts only if he had a legal duty to act

met
4. Hutchins

12
Did the Chain Break?
  • The crew's failures were responsive, not coincidental: they arose from the same gun and safety system
  • Responsive causes do not break the chain unless abnormal and unforeseeable
  • People v. Kibbe: should the death have been foreseen as reasonably related to Baldwin's acts?
13
Mens Rea

Recklessness

Aware of the risk and consciously disregards it → manslaughter (MPC § 210.3)
Did Baldwin know the gun might be loaded?

Negligence

Fails to perceive a risk he should have perceived → negligent homicide (§ 210.4); People v. Baker
Or did he reasonably trust the “cold gun” call?
New Mexico: involuntary manslaughter requires criminal negligence, not ordinary carelessness (NMSA § 30-2-3(B); State v. Yarborough, 1996)
14
German Law,
§ 222 StGB
§
1Causing a death by negligence, up to 5 years in prison or a fine
2Would a careful person in his position have acted differently?
3He thought the gun held only dummies, so no intent (§ 16 StGB)
4Ordinary negligence is enough in Germany, while New Mexico requires criminal negligence
SOURCESStGB §§ 15, 16, 222 · Dubber and Hörnle, Criminal Law (2014) pp 233, 243 to 245, 579, 590 · Fedorczyk, Sessions 11 and 12 · NPR (AP) 31 Jan 2024 · State v. Gutierrez, proposed jury instructions (2024)

Whose risk
was it?
  • Risk realised: the death is what gun-safety rules aim to prevent
  • Principle of trust: you may rely on others doing their job, if you do yours and have no serious reason to doubt them
  • German question: in whose sphere was the risk?
The crew's sphere
Armourer + assistant director
  • What is in the gun
  • Checking the rounds
  • The “cold gun” call
Trust applies ✓Bulletin #1: guns are her job
Principle of trustVertrauensgrundsatz
Baldwin's sphere
(if the State's evidence holds)
  • Where it is aimed
  • Finger on the trigger
Trust does not apply ✗his own duty of care
One result
Halyna Hutchins dies
Trust has limitsEarlier discharges, crew walkout: warning signs, but nothing shows he knew
18
Liable in
Germany?
  • Step 1, shown previously: negligence. Step 2: is the death imputed to him?
  • Liable under § 222, plus § 229 for Souza: likely a fine, a suspended sentence or a § 153a StPO dismissal
  • Easier than in New Mexico, but a similar result: Germany reasons from the risk, not foreseeability
